findings.reason: the operative rule is the sentence's own "the node computes the interval for the number it tests and reports it", so the number is only an illustration and a 3 % looser band does not alter what the section delivers.
findings.text: the illustrative interval "about 0.72 to 1.32 for six directions" is not the interval for six directions: the exact Bonferroni interval for 255 degrees of freedom at 99 % joint coverage is 0.745–1.302 for six directions, and 0.72–1.32 is roughly what fifteen to eighteen directions give, so a reader treating the printed band as the operative six-direction band tests about 3 % too loosely

findings.reason: the clause is a harmless extra check, the reduced-chi-square half of clause (1) already surfaces any real bias, and removing or tightening it would not change what the node builds or how the section is judged.
findings.text: clause (2)'s first half, "the mean of the recovered coefficients lies within three standard errors of the generating coefficients on every state", cannot fail as §6 specifies its fit: the noise is fixed zero-mean Gaussian and the fit is given exactly those standard deviations as its weights, and weighted least squares with correct weights is unbiased by construction, so the 256-realisation mean sits at the generating coefficients whatever the residual code does
